question.text:
$2$ is prime, or $14$ is a multiple of $7$ and $5.$

Express the compound statement above in symbolic form given the following notations:

  • $R: \textrm{$2$ is prime}$

  • $S: \textrm{$14$ is a multiple of $7$}$

  • $T: \textrm{$14$ is a multiple of $5$}$
question.explanation:
The word "and" is represented by the symbol "$\land$", while the word "or" is represented by the symbol "$\lor$".

Note that this sentence consists of two parts:

  • Part 1: $2$ is prime. This corresponds to $R.$

  • Part 2: $14$ is a multiple of $7$ and $5.$ This corresponds to \[ \underbrace{14 \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is a multiple of }7 }_S \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{and}}_{\land} \quad \underbrace{14 \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is a multiple of }5 }_T, \] that is, $S \land T.$

So, we can express the sentence as \[ \underbrace{2 \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is prime} }_R \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{or}}_{\lor} \quad \underbrace{14 \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is a multiple of } 7 \textbf{ and } 5 }_{S \, \land \, T}, \]

that is, $R \lor (S \land T).$

example.title: Expressing Nested Compound Statements in Symbolic Form

question.text:
\[ \underbrace{\sqrt{2} \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is irrational}}_A \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{or}}_{\lor} \quad \underbrace{1-2=1}_B \]

For the compound statement above, we have that
question.explanation:
First, let's recall the following facts about the "and" $(\land)$ and "or" $(\lor)$ logical connectives:

  • The statement $A \land B$ is true if both $A$ and $B$ are true.

  • The statement $A \lor B$ is true if either $A$ is true, or $B$ is true, or both $A$ and $B$ are true.

In our case, $A$ is true, and $B$ is false. Therefore, the result is true:

\begin{align*} \underbrace{ \sqrt{2} \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is irrational} }_A \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{or}}_{\lor} \quad \underbrace{1-2=1}_B &\:\:\equiv\: \text{true} \lor \textrm{false} \equiv \textrm{true} \end{align*}

example.title: Finding Truth Values of Compound Statements

question.text:
$\sqrt{5}$ is rational, or $3|12$ and $3|18.$

Express the compound statement above in symbolic form given the following notations:

  • $P: \textrm{$\sqrt{5}$ is rational}$

  • $Q: \textrm{$3|12$}$

  • $R: \textrm{$3|18$ }$
question.explanation:
The word "and" is represented by the symbol "$\land$", while the word "or" is represented by the symbol "$\lor$".

Note that this sentence consists of two parts:

  • Part 1: $\sqrt{5}$ is rational. This corresponds to $P.$

  • Part 2: $3|12$ and $3|18.$ This corresponds to \[ \underbrace{3 \vphantom{p}|12 }_Q \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{and}}_{\land} \quad \underbrace{3 \vphantom{p}|18 }_R, \] that is, $Q \land R.$

So, we can express the sentence as \[ \underbrace{\sqrt{5} \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is rational} }_P \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{or}}_{\lor} \quad \underbrace{3 \vphantom{p}|12 \textbf{ and } 3|18 }_{Q \, \land \, R}, \] that is, $P \lor (Q \land R).$

example.title: Expressing Nested Compound Statements in Symbolic Form

question.text:
\[ \underbrace{0 \vphantom{|}\textrm{ is even}}_P \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{|}\textbf{or}}_{\lor}\quad \underbrace{ \overbrace{\{1,2\}\cap\{1\}=\{1,2\}}^Q \quad \overbrace{\vphantom{|}\textbf{or}}^{\lor} \quad \overbrace{\dfrac23 \vphantom{|}\textrm{ is irrational}}^R }_{Q \, \lor \, R} \]

For the compound statement above, we have that
question.explanation:
First, let's recall the following facts about the "and" $(\land)$ and "or" $(\lor)$ logical connectives:

  • The statement $A \land B$ is true if both $A$ and $B$ are true.

  • The statement $A \lor B$ is true if either $A$ is true, or $B$ is true, or both $A$ and $B$ are true.

In our case, $P$ is true, $Q$ is false, and $R$ is false. Therefore, $Q \lor R$ is false, but the result is true: \begin{align*} P \lor (Q\lor R) &\equiv\text{true} \lor \overbrace{(\textrm{false} \lor \textrm{false})}^{\textrm{false}} \\[5pt] &\equiv \textrm{true} \lor \textrm{false} \\[3pt] &\equiv \textrm{true} \end{align*}

example.title: Finding Truth Values of Complex Statements

question.text:
\[ \underbrace{2 \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is negative} }_A \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{or}}_{\lor} \quad \underbrace{0.5 \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is rational} }_B \]

For the compound statement above, we have that
question.explanation:
First, let's recall the following facts about the "and" $(\land)$ and "or" $(\lor)$ logical connectives:

  • The statement $A \land B$ is true if both $A$ and $B$ are true.

  • The statement $A \lor B$ is true if either $A$ is true, or $B$ is true, or both $A$ and $B$ are true.

In our case, $A$ is false, and $B$ is true. Therefore, the result is true:

\begin{align*} \underbrace{2 \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is negative} }_A \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{or}}_{\lor} \quad \underbrace{0.5 \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is rational} }_B &\:\:\equiv\: \text{false} \lor \textrm{true} \equiv \textrm{true} \end{align*}
